newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Demand for Bulgaria short-term deposits rises.
newsitem.headline: Demand for Bulgaria short-term deposits rises.

text.p: Demand for short-term deposits rose due to treasury paper payments but the lev funds rates were unchanged as supply was high enough, dealers said.
"Some banks bid for deposits of up to three days as their liquidity tightened after Thursday's payment of treasury notes bought last Friday," said a dealer.
Banks bought three-year notes worth 35 billion levs on July 11. This issue's settlement date was July 17.
Overnight interbank depo rates stood at 2.0-2.4 percent annual, flat from Thursday. Spot week rates were also unchanged at 4.0-5.0 percent.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 2.46 percent on Thursday against 2.28 percent on Wednesday, a central bank official said.
The central bank said on Thursday it would cut its simple annual main rate to 6.12 percent from 6.96 percent, effective from July 21.
